newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore opposition party faces watershed hearing.
newsitem.headline: Singapore opposition party faces watershed hearing.

text.p: The fate of the opposition Singapore Democratic Party (SDP) hung in the balance on Thursday as its leader and three other party members faced charges of contempt at a special parliamentary committee hearing.

Trenchant government critic SDP Secretary-General Chee Soon Juan and his colleagues could be fined or jailed if the Committee of Privileges, which began hearing evidence from Chee on Thursday, finds the opposition members guilty.
Chee and the others, none of whom are MPs, could also be barred from contesting future elections if the committee decides to pass on the case to a civil court and it finds against them.
Seven of the eight members of parliament (MPs) on the committee are from the ruling People's Action Party.

The opposition won only four of the 81 parliamentary seats in the last general election in 1991. The SDP took three of those four and gained an average of between 48 and 49 percent of the vote in the handful of seats it contested.
Chee has the highest profile in the SDP and is widely expected to run for parliament in the next election. Political analysts say his elimination as a political figure would badly damage the party.

The hearing, which comes ahead of elections that must be held by April 1997, was called after a complaint by Health Minister George Yeo that Chee and his colleagues lied to a Select Committee on health care.

An SDP document submitted to the committee in August had claimed government spending on health care had fallen to just five percent of Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) in the 1990s from around 40 percent in the 1970s.
The SDP later admitted the figure for the 1990s was incorrect and should have been 25.4 percent,
Facing charges of perjury, prevarication, misconduct and wilfully giving false evidence, Chee told the hearing the figure was a typing mistake and a result of human error.
"I deny the allegation that I have presented false documents to the Select Committee with the intent to deceive," Chee told the hearing on Thursday. "There was a typographical error."
Questioning of the other three SDP defendants, Wong Hong Toy, S. Kunalen and Kwan Yue Keng, began in late afternoon and was expected to continue for a second day.
If found guilty, the men could be fined up to Singapore $50,000 (US $35,460) each and jailed until parliament is dissolved.
